messages:
nora: Quick note from the split-session: DNS is the trickiest part when we separate customer CP into private control planes. tossing up a proposal for delegated resolution.

sam: tl;dr?

nora: idea: instead of modifying tenant VPC resolvers, we publish a per-tenant delegation zone we control (e.g., tenant-<id>.cp.redwood-internal) and program the private endpoint to resolve via that zone. this avoids touching customer resolvers.

eli: so tenants still query their usual suffix but we rewrite at the ENI? how does it look on the wire?

nora: flow: tenant service -> normal VPC resolver -> conditional forwarder for *.cp.redwood-internal -> our resolver in-region -> answers pointing at private endpoint IPs. no route-table changes.

tasha: advantage: we can atomically switch records for migrations. downside: customers with strict DNS policies might block conditional forwarding.

sam: do we have authority to add conditional forwarders in customer accounts? many don't allow changes.
nora: that's the point: we don't change customer resolver configs. we host a delegation subdomain under their control by provisioning a private hosted zone in their account and setting the VPC association during onboarding. minimal terraform step.

eli: provisioning private hosted zones per-tenant adds to our infra quota. can we instead use a central shared zone and namespaced records? e.g., tenants.priv-cp.redwood. That avoids many hosted zones but leaks cross-tenant visibility risk.

tasha: visibility risk is real. shared zone records could be enumerated if someone gains list-zone perms. prefer tenant-scoped private hosted zones for isolation.

sam: operationally, what about failover when private CP is down? who answers the delegation?
nora: our resolver cluster will expose health-aware answers. fallback: if tenant CP down -> return relay A IP with explicit TTL and also emit metric dns_delegation_fallback{tenant}. clients then hit relay.

eli: TTLs? short TTLs cause load, long TTLs delay cutover. propose 30s for delegation records during cutovers, 300s normal.
tasha: add guardrail: during mass migration we rate-limit DNS change pushes to avoid API quota storms.

sam: security: ensure hosted zone creation requires tenant-kept ownership tag and we don't store zone secrets in plaintext. also rotate any route53-assume-role creds.
nora: noted. we'll require ephemeral creds scoped per-tenant with short TTL and audit logs.

infra-bot: reminder: onboarding playbook checklist updated: private-hosted-zone creation step added. (link)

eli: small compatibility note: some legacy connectors do DNS caching at app level. document a client-side invalidation recommendation and include header X-CP-Transition in fallback responses so we can debug stale caches.

nora: next actions: I'll add a diagram to the RFC follow-up, include Terraform snippet, and a runbook step for rollback. posting draft in 24h. thanks y'all.
